findings.finding: Sets RLB before PMP reconfiguration (line 139), programs M-only firmware regions before enabling MML (lines 144-180), writes pmpaddr-before-pmpcfg via pmp_set(), keeps RLB set for dynamic mappings (line 215), and issues sfence.vma after all entries are programmed (line 216). Correctly handles the three PMP programming phases: RLB-set, M-only region programming, MML-enable, then shared/SU region programming. No window exists where a partially-overlapping PMP entry could fault M-mode firmware access.
findings.snippet:
csr_set(CSR_MSECCFG, MSECCFG_RLB);  // line 139
csr_set(CSR_MSECCFG, MSECCFG_MML);   // line 185
sbi_hart_pmp_fence();                 // line 216

findings.finding: Boot-time check that mseccfg.MML==0 before OpenSBI configures PMP. If a previous boot stage left MML=1, PMP registers may be locked, preventing OpenSBI from establishing its own firmware-region entries. Returning SBI_EILL prevents the exact scenario in the security spec where pre-existing locked PMP entries could overlap/block M-mode firmware access.

Correct atomic write ordering: pmpaddr CSR is written first (line 377), then pmpcfg CSR (line 378). The address-matching bits (PMP_A) are only activated by the pmpcfg write. Between the two writes, the old pmpcfg (read at line 360) controls matching — if old A bits were 0, the new pmpaddr is irrelevant; if old A bits were non-zero for the same entry index, the entry was already active and is being reprogrammed within its own slot. No cross-entry contamination. The NAPOT encoding at lines 364-374 correctly handles pmpaddr bit layout including the all-ones case for full-address-space coverage.
findings.snippet:
csr_write_num(pmpaddr_csr, pmpaddr);  // line 377
csr_write_num(pmpcfg_csr, pmpcfg);    // line 378

findings.finding: Preserves firmware PMP entries during domain context switch: iterates through all PMP entries but skips those identified as firmware regions (line 306). This ensures M-mode code executing the unconfigure/configure transition itself never loses access to firmware code/data memory. Without this guard, disabling firmware PMP entries would trigger the exact self-fault scenario in the security spec.

Issues sfence.vma (and hfence.gvma if H-extension present) to flush cached virtual-address and PMP translations after PMP state changes. Correct per Priv spec 1.12 §3.7.2, which warns that PMP translations can be speculatively cached. Called after both oldpmp_configure (line 296) and smepmp_configure (line 216).

Saves MENVCFG (containing ENVCFG_STCE for SSTC delegation), MIE, MIP (S-mode bits only: SSIP|STIP), MEDELEG, and MIDELEG across non-retentive suspend. This ensures timer interrupt delivery via SSTC and trap delegation are correctly restored after warm resume. Without saving MENVCFG, S-mode would lose stimecmp access after resume, breaking timer interrupts.

Restores MENVCFG (STCE), MIDELEG, MEDELEG, MIE, and re-injects saved MIP_STIP after non-retentive suspend resume. Restores MENVCFG before other CSRs (line 441) — correct ordering since MENVCFG controls which CSRs are accessible. Re-injects STIP via csr_set (line 445), which is safe because STIP is an S-mode writable bit in MIP.
findings.snippet:
csr_write64(CSR_MENVCFG, hdata->saved_menvcfg);  // line 441
csr_set(CSR_MIP, (hdata->saved_mip & (MIP_SSIP | MIP_STIP)));  // line 445

findings.finding: Writes CSR_STIMECMP directly when SSTC available (line 142). M-mode writes to delegated S-mode CSRs are permitted by hardware. No SFENCE.VMA needed — STIMECMP is a timer CSR, not a VM/PMP CSR. The csr_write64 handles both RV32 (word-at-a-time STIMECMP/STIMECMPH) and RV64 correctly.

Sets ENVCFG_STCE in CSR_MENVCFG when SSTC extension detected, delegating stimecmp CSR to S-mode. The write happens during cold boot init sequence, after feature detection but before entering S-mode. Safe: the csr_write64 at line 174 writes the fully constructed menvcfg_val including STCE along with other bits (Zicboz, Svpbmt, etc.) in one atomic CSR write.

Clears MIP_MTIP from MIE (line 152) and only injects MIP_STIP when SSTC is NOT available (lines 158-159). With SSTC, timer interrupts go directly to S-mode via stimecmp hardware comparison; M-mode injection of STIP would cause a spurious double-interrupt. The conditional correctly respects the SSTC delegation model.

Domain context switch: unconfigures then reconfigures PMP (lines 127-128). Between these calls, firmware PMP entries are preserved by sbi_hart_pmp_unconfigure which skips firmware regions. After PMP reconfiguration, S-mode CSRs are swapped (sstatus/sie/stvec/satp/etc.) followed by sfence.vma (line 140) to flush stale TLB entries from the old domain's virtual address space. This is correct: PMP is reconfigured first, then virtual memory context is swapped with appropriate fence.

Configures mideleg/medeleg before entering S-mode: delegates SSIP/STIP/SEIP interrupts and supervisor-level exceptions (misaligned fetch, breakpoint, ECALL, page faults). Writes mideleg (line 248) then medeleg (line 249) — ordering does not create a security window since these are write-only configuration CSRs. If H-extension is present, additionally delegates VS-level exceptions (guest page faults, virtual supervisor ecall). Correctly gates on misa_extension('S') at line 217 — mideleg/medeleg don't exist without S-mode.
findings.snippet:
csr_write(CSR_MIDELEG, interrupts);   // line 248
csr_write(CSR_MEDELEG, exceptions);    // line 249

findings.finding: Clears PMP_A bits for entry N via read-modify-write on the containing pmpcfg CSR. The cfgmask isolates the target entry's byte (line 309), preserving bits for all other entries in the same register. Note: pmpaddr is NOT cleared — the address register retains its old value. This is safe because without A bits set, the pmpaddr value is ignored by hardware. The pmpaddr will be overwritten when the entry is later re-enabled via pmp_set() which writes pmpaddr before pmpcfg.

Probes PMP presence during hart_detect_features by writing CSR_PMPCFG0 (value 0) then CSR_PMPADDR0 (PMP_ADDR_MASK). This happens during cold boot BEFORE any PMP entries are configured for firmware protection — so there are no active firmware entries to corrupt. The probe writes and reads back PMP registers to determine pmp_count and pmp_log2gran. Any residual PMP state from a previous boot stage will be fully overwritten by subsequent sbi_hart_smepmp_configure.

Non-Smepmp PMP configuration: programs entries one-by-one via pmp_set(). In old PMP mode (no MML), M-mode accesses always succeed when no PMP entry matches — M-mode privilege exemption applies. The security spec concern about byte-range match superseding M-mode privilege only applies under Smepmp (MML=1). This path is therefore inherently safe from the self-fault scenario. Correctly issues sbi_hart_pmp_fence() at line 296.
findings.snippet:
pmp_set(pmp_idx++, pmp_flags, reg->base, reg->order);  // per-entry
sbi_hart_pmp_fence();  // line 296

findings.finding: Translates domain memregion flags to Smepmp pmpcfg encoding. Validates that M-only regions never have RWX permissions (lines 187-192) — under Smepmp, M-mode RWX on a region is not a valid encoding. For shared regions, correctly encodes the Smepmp bit patterns (L+R+W+X combos) per the MML=1 pmpcfg encoding table in the RISC-V spec. Pure data transformation with no CSR access.

Enables S-mode seed CSR access via MSECCFG_SSEED (set) and MSECCFG_USEED (clear) when Zkr extension present. These are entropy-source configuration bits in mseccfg, unrelated to PMP protection. The csr_set/csr_clear operations are atomic and affect only the seed-related bits.
